events.region: Southwest Mountains; Lower Rio Grande Valley; South Central Highlands; San Agustin Plains and Adjacent Lowlands
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1041 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from 28 miles south of National Radio
Astronomy Observatory to 18 miles south of Bosque Del Apache Refuge,
moving north at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Socorro, Magdalena, San Antonio, Bosque Del Apache Refuge,
Escondida, Lemitar, Luis Lopez and Laborcita.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 380 between Mile Markers 1 and 15. Highway 60 between Mile
Markers 107 and 138. Interstate 25 between Mile Markers 124 and 157.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Wasatch Plateau/Book Cliffs; Central Mountains; Castle Country; San Rafael Swell
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, San Rafael Swell and Wasatch
Plateau/Book Cliffs.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A widespread area of light to moderate rainfall will move through
the area tonight, helping to the keep the area saturated and more
easily prone to flooding. Additional showers and thunderstorms
capable of heavy rainfall are expected Thursday afternoon and
evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Pima County in southeastern Arizona...
South Central Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 1030 PM MST.

* At 927 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated between 1 and 1.5 inches of
rain had fallen this evening. Flash flooding is ongoing, especially
along the Brawley Wash.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. This
excessive rainfall will continue to drain into the Brawley
Wash.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marana, Avra Valley, Pinal Airpark, Picacho Peak State Park, Red
Rock and Dove Mountain.

This includes Interstate 10 between mile markers 218 and 239.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Sasco Rd at Santa Cruz Wash.
